business_problem: E-commerce companies can ship perishable goods anywhere in the U.S. if they have a good handle on logistics.
solution_summary: Grip built its Databricks implementation around Databricks Data + AI Platform, Databricks SQL, Unity Catalog, Lakeflow Connect. E-commerce companies can ship perishable goods anywhere in the U.S. if they have a good handle on logistics. Databricks Data + AI Platform provides the shared lakehouse environment for ingestion, engineering, analytics, and AI workflows in this deployment. Databricks SQL serves governed analytics, dashboards, and ad hoc queries for business users and operational teams. Unity Catalog applies centralized governance, lineage, auditing, and access control across shared data assets. Lakeflow Connect ingests source data from operational systems into governed lakehouse tables. The solution also connects to Shopify, ShipStation, Zendesk, Dynamics, so teams can work from a shared governed environment instead of disconnected tools. Databricks makes it easy for Grip to do everything with one set of tools.

data_flow: Source data and events are ingested through managed connectors, files, or streaming feeds into databricks, curated in shared lakehouse tables, processed with Databricks compute and orchestration services, and served through analytics, semantic search, or model endpoints for downstream users and applications. It connects with Shopify, ShipStation, Zendesk.
business_outcome: Databricks makes it easy for Grip to do everything with one set of tools. The Grip team can build machine learning models and data engineering pipelines end to end, serve end users with analytics, and track internal analytics — all within one platform.
